before_times: Which appliance, and its brand: a fridge, freezer, washer, dryer, dishwasher, range, oven or cooktop
Gas or electric, for a range, oven or dryer
What it's doing, since when, and any error code on the display
Bought when, and any warranty: the maker's, a store plan or a home warranty, or not sure
At the shop: which small appliance, its brand, and what it's doing
after_time: Who will be home: the customer, or another adult (their name and mobile go on the secure page)
Can the appliance be reached and pulled out, and is there room behind it
Own or rent, and who pays: the customer, or the landlord or manager
A home warranty or store plan: its name, so the owner can check it
secure_page_only: The appliance's label photo (brand, model and serial): it tells the tech which parts fit and dates the appliance
The landlord's or manager's name and mobile
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the owner of the home names may book for them.

stop.words: A gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm (a gas range, oven or dryer)
stop.says: Leave the house now and keep everyone out. Don't flip switches, unplug anything or use a phone inside. Once outside, call 911 and the gas company.
stop.booking: No booking. A new request must say the gas company cleared the home.

stop.says: Get everyone out now. Once outside, call 911. Don't go back in.
stop.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

go_on.words: Sparks or a burning smell from an appliance
go_on.says: Unplug it, or switch off its breaker, only if that's safe. Don't use it until it's fixed.

go_on.words: Water near outlets (a washer, a dishwasher, a fridge's water line)
go_on.says: Stay away from wet outlets and cords. Turn off the appliance's water supply if you can reach it without touching the water.

safety_and_stop_words.always: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

prep: A fridge that isn't cooling: leave it plugged in and don't defrost it. The frost shows what failed. Move food to a cooler.
Clear a path to the appliance, and space to pull it out
A washer or dishwasher with water in it: leave the water in, and put towels down
At the shop: bring the appliance with all its parts, like the bowl, the lid and the cord

staff.supervision: A trainee works only alongside a tech. A trainee is never sent alone, and never opens a sealed system.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit, built-in and commercial jobs, and same-day jobs. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
staff.stand_in: Another tech with the same skills, at the same window and price. A sealed-system job only goes to another tech with an EPA card.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. A renter books, and the landlord or manager OKs it where they pay. A person the owner of the home names may book for them.

visit.done: The tech runs the appliance with the customer, then texts DONE with the bill's lines.
visit.changes_at_visit: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A bigger job found, like a sealed-system repair, gets its own quote.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Most states don't license appliance repair. Some register repair companies, and some cities license repair shops: the state's or city's form says. Refrigeration work and gas or electric hookups can need that trade's own license.
license.who: The company, where the state registers repair companies. Each tech, only for what their own card or license covers: an EPA refrigerant card for sealed systems, and a refrigeration or gas license where the state asks.
ask: The company's repair registration or license number, where the state's form asks for one
Each tech's EPA refrigerant card number and type, for anyone who opens a sealed system
Each tech's refrigeration or gas license, where the state's form asks, in their invite reply
A maker's authorized-servicer number, only if the business takes that maker's warranty jobs
license.insurance: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.
license.background: Only where the state's form asks.

never_in_a_text: Gate or lock codes, card details, the label photo's serial number, and photos from inside the home: these stay on the secure page.
